places.description: America's first living-history museum, built in 1930 to recreate a 1630 Puritan settlement — thatched cottages, wigwams, and a blacksmith's forge — in Forest River Park. Seasonal and ticketed.
places.name: Pioneer Village
Turner's Seafood
places.description: Fresh fish and a raw bar in historic Lyceum Hall — the very room where Alexander Graham Bell is said to have given one of his first public telephone demonstrations.

places.name: Salem Public Library
places.description: Salem's public library since 1889, housed in the elegant Italianate mansion of sea captain John Bertram, whose family gave their grand Essex Street home to the city.

places.name: The Tavern
places.description: The cozy, oak-paneled tavern inside the historic 1925 Hawthorne Hotel, serving chowder, burgers, and local drafts within view of Salem Common.

places.name: Peabody Essex Museum
places.description: Rooted in a 1799 sea-captains' society, the Peabody Essex is among America's oldest and finest museums, with world-class Asian and maritime art and a 200-year-old house brought whole from China.

places.name: Salem Willows Beach
places.description: A small sandy-and-pebble beach tucked into Salem Willows Park, with calm, clear water and harbor views. Swimming is unguarded but it's a beloved warm-weather spot.

places.name: Artist's Row
places.description: A small brick pedestrian plaza off Derby Square where local artisans sell jewelry, ceramics, and crafts from seasonal stalls, with a bite to eat and public restrooms close at hand.

places.name: Bewitched Statue of Elizabeth Montgomery
places.description: A bronze of Elizabeth Montgomery as Samantha from the sitcom Bewitched, perched on her broom beneath a crescent moon. Unveiled by the TV Land network in 2005 in Lappin Park.

places.name: Central Wharf
places.description: An 1780s Salem Maritime wharf once among the port's largest, its vanished warehouse footprint outlined in stone and its surviving brick store now serving as a park information center.

places.name: The House Of The Seven Gables
places.description: The 1668 seaside mansion that inspired Hawthorne's novel — among New England's oldest surviving wooden houses, with a secret staircase and the author's birthplace moved onto its grounds.

places.name: Witch Mansion
places.description: An indoor haunted house on Essex Street full of animatronics and illusions, where visitors choose their own scare level. Open select days, and daily through October.

places.name: Jaho
places.description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

places.name: Gulu-Gulu Cafe
places.description: A European-style café and bar on the Essex Street pedestrian mall, pouring Belgian beers and serving crepes and paninis, with live music most nights of the week.

places.name: Divinations - Psychic Parlor and Learning Center
New England Pirate Museum
places.description: A guided romp through a recreated colonial seaport, a boardable pirate ship, and an eighty-foot cave, telling the tales of New England's real buccaneers. Seasonal.

places.name: Hex Old World Witchery
places.description: Salem's largest witchcraft shop, dealing in 'Old World' herbs, potions, brooms, and candles. Founded by warlock Christian Day, it draws famously long lines come October.

places.name: Brew Box
places.description: A tiny downtown café known for seasonal lattes and house-made treats — breakfast burritos, pop-tarts, and cinnamon rolls — to fuel a morning of sightseeing.

places.name: Finz Seafood & Grill
places.description: A harborfront seafood restaurant and raw bar on Pickering Wharf, serving sustainably minded fish with wide-open views of Salem Harbor.

places.name: The Red Line Cafe
places.description: A cozy downtown breakfast-and-lunch café known for pressed paninis, savory crepes, salads, and good coffee, with free Wi-Fi for lingering.

places.name: Custom House
places.description: The stately 1819 Federal building where duties were levied at the height of Salem's shipping boom. Nathaniel Hawthorne worked here, and it opens the long introduction to his novel The Scarlet Letter.
Salem's longest-running haunted house, founded in 1993, offering a live 'ghoulish guide,' a vampire-led ghost walk, and fireside ghost stories, with frights you can dial up or down.
places.name: Chambers of Terror

places.description: The original location of a beloved New England vegetarian café, serving organic grain-and-veggie bowls, wraps, and smoothies on Essex Street.
places.name: Life Alive Organic Cafe
Salem Witch Trials Memorial
places.description: A solemn memorial dedicated in 1992 beside the old Charter Street cemetery, its low granite walls lined with benches naming each 1692 victim and inscribed with their pleas of innocence, cut off mid-sentence in stone.

places.name: A&J King Artisan Bakers
places.description: An acclaimed Central Street bakery and café since 2006, turning out sourdough and country breads, pastries, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches.

places.name: International Monster Museum
places.description: A lantern-lit walk through the world's monsters, cryptids, and folklore creatures, built by international effects artists. Equal parts museum and jump-scare.
A tidy North Salem waterfront playground with a picnic pavilion, dog area, and water views where children can watch the commuter trains roll past across the cove.
places.name: Furlong Park

places.description: Salem's oldest witch shop, opened in 1971 by the city's famous witch Laurie Cabot. Behind its black-and-purple storefront wait spell kits, tarot, crystals, and psychic readings.
places.name: Crow Haven Corner
First Church in Salem, Unitarian Universalist

places.description: A leafy district of Federal-era mansions named for Salem's own woodcarver and architect Samuel McIntire, with Chestnut Street long counted among the most beautiful streets in America.
places.name: McIntire Historic District

places.description: Actresses reenact a witch-trial scene drawn from the 1692 court records, after which a guide leads you through a recreated dungeon — a theatrical retelling of Salem's darkest year.
places.name: Witch Dungeon Museum
Vampfangs
places.description: The only dedicated vampire shop in New England, fitting Salem with custom fangs since 1993 alongside gothic fashion, fragrance, and a curated shelf of metaphysical goods.

places.name: Forest River Park
places.description: A waterfront park with two beaches, a community pool, and harbor-view picnic hills — also home to Pioneer Village, the recreated 1630 Puritan settlement.

places.name: Notch Brewing
places.description: A brewery and waterfront beer garden on the South River specializing in Czech- and German-style session lagers, poured from North America's first Czech side-pour taps.

places.name: Settler
places.description: An intimate, wine-forward small-plates spot with Mediterranean leanings — house sourdough, whipped ricotta, and crudo. Reservations are a good idea.

places.name: Salem Witch Museum
places.description: Salem's most-visited attraction, where a thirteen-scene narrated stage show inside a Gothic former church dramatizes the events of 1692. A second exhibit traces the changing face of the witch.

places.name: Halloween Museum
places.description: A year-round, family-friendly museum tracing Halloween's history and pop culture, complete with blacklit 3D rooms and photo-ready tributes to favorite spooky films.

places.name: The Lost Museum
places.description: A theatrical walk through a 'cabinet of oddities' supposedly lost in Salem's great fire of 1914, with living portraits and special effects. A guided, October-only experience.

places.name: Witch House
places.description: The dark, gabled home of trial judge Jonathan Corwin, built around 1675 — the only structure still standing in Salem with direct ties to the 1692 witch trials, now a house museum.

places.name: Ropes Mansion
places.description: A grand Georgian mansion of about 1727 on Essex Street, with a free formal garden, kept by the Peabody Essex Museum. Fans know its exterior as Allison's house in Hocus Pocus.

places.name: Bit Bar Salem
places.description: A retro arcade bar on Derby Street pairing classic cabinets and pinball with craft beer and kitchen fare. Twenty-one-plus after dark, and closed Mondays.

places.name: The Roof
places.description: Salem's only open-air rooftop bar, atop the boutique Hotel Salem, with cocktails, tacos, and views over downtown. Open seasonally.

places.name: Bambolina
places.description: A wood-fired Neapolitan pizzeria on Derby Street that shares its kitchen with a ramen counter, so a blistered pie can come with a bowl of noodles on the side.

places.name: Village Tavern
places.description: An upbeat American tavern across from the Peabody Essex, with three bars, a deep craft-beer list, locally loved burgers, and a patio.

places.name: Winter Island Park
places.description: A 54-acre former military outpost on Salem Harbor with a beach, boat ramp, and campground, plus the 1871 Fort Pickering Lighthouse and the earthworks of a colonial-era fort.

places.name: Immaculate Conception Church - Mary Queen of the Apostles Parish
Ledger Restaurant & Bar
places.description: Upscale progressive New England dining inside an 1818 bank, where the old vault is now a wine room and the teller windows survive as decor.

places.name: Pickering Wharf Marina
places.description: A waterfront village of shops, restaurants, and a working marina, built in the 1970s in eighteenth-century style at the gateway to Salem's historic harbor.

places.name: Odd Meter Coffee Co.
places.description: A small, serious downtown coffee bar run by a father-and-son team, pouring single-origin batch brew and craft espresso for the specialty-coffee crowd.

places.name: Dire Wolf Tavern
places.description: A saloon-styled tavern on Washington Street serving elevated comfort food and award-winning sushi, with a hidden speakeasy, Hallowed Ground, tucked downstairs.

places.name: Nathaniel Hawthorne Statue
places.description: A seated bronze of Salem's most famous author, sculpted by Bela Lyon Pratt and dedicated in 1925 on Hawthorne Boulevard, near the streets that shaped his dark New England tales.

places.name: Wolf Next Door Coffee
places.description: An earth-minded neighborhood coffee shop in the historic Derby Street district, with organic coffee, pastries, and breakfast sandwiches, indoors or out.

places.name: Proctor's Ledge Memorial
places.description: A quiet semicircular memorial at the foot of Gallows Hill marking the spot, confirmed by researchers in 2016, where nineteen people were hanged in 1692. Each victim's name is carved in stone.

places.name: Mahi Mahi Harbor Cruises & Private Events
Waikiki Beach At Winter Island Park
Flying Saucer Pizza Company
places.description: New York-style pizza in a sci-fi-themed parlor packed with Doctor Who and Star Wars decor, the dough made fresh in-house every day.

places.name: Real Pirates Salem
places.description: A pirate museum built around real treasure from the Whydah, the wrecked ship of pirate 'Black Sam' Bellamy — the world's only authenticated pirate hoard.

places.name: Old Town Hall
places.description: Salem's oldest surviving public building (1816), presiding over Derby Square. Fans know it as the Hocus Pocus Halloween party hall, where the Sanderson sisters cast their spell on the crowd with 'I Put a Spell on You.'

places.name: Waterfront Park
places.description: A small green space along Derby Street's harborfront, a quiet place to take in the boats and water between Salem's busier wharves.

places.name: Salem Willows Park
places.description: A breezy seaside park since 1858, named for its old willow trees, with vintage arcades, a band shell, harbor views, and the popcorn-and-chowder stands of a classic New England amusement grove.

places.name: Blackcraft Coffee
places.description: A goth-branded coffee bar tucked inside the Blackcraft apparel shop, serving Salem-themed specialty drinks amid the alt-fashion racks.

places.name: Salem Common
places.description: The roughly nine-acre green at the heart of the city, a designated militia training field since 1714 and now a tree-lined park ringed by historic homes and centered on its 1926 bandstand.
Marks the North Bridge site of 1775's 'Leslie's Retreat,' a bloodless standoff where townsfolk turned back British troops hunting hidden cannon, weeks before the shots at Lexington.
places.name: Leslie's Retreat Monument
St Vasilios (Basil) the Great Greek Orthodox Church
Gallows Hill
places.description: The hill long assumed to be the witch-trial execution ground, though the hangings in fact took place downhill at Proctor's Ledge. Today it's a neighborhood park with views over the city.
A mad-scientist haunt beneath the Salem Wax Museum, winding past live actors and animatronics. Its expanded 'Laboratory of Terror' wing adds a longer, more interactive descent.
places.name: Frankenstein's Laboratory

places.description: A bright, modern take on the witch shop, stocking candles, crystals, and home goods from independent makers, plus workshops and readings — witchcraft by way of contemporary design.
places.name: Hauswitch

places.description: The National Park Service's regional visitor center, set in an 1890s armory drill shed. Exhibits and an orientation film introduce Salem Maritime and the wider Essex Heritage area.
places.name: Salem Visitor's Center

places.description: A serious traditional occult shop near the Common, lined with candles, herbs, and rare spellbooks, with a roster of readers. A favorite of practitioners over souvenir-seekers.
places.name: The Cauldron Black
Roger Conant Statue
places.description: A cloaked, broad-hatted bronze of Salem's Puritan founder, who led the 1626 settlement at Naumkeag. Brooding atop a boulder near the Common, it's often mistaken for a witch.

places.name: Palmer Cove Park
places.description: A neighborhood park in The Point with ball courts, a playing field, community gardens, and waterfront paths — a recently revamped pocket of green beside the harbor.

places.name: Mercy Tavern
places.description: A lively Derby Street gastropub with globe-spanning comfort food and the longest live-music tradition in Salem, with a kitchen that runs late.

places.name: A&J King Artisan Bakers
places.description: An acclaimed Central Street bakery and café since 2006, turning out sourdough and country breads, pastries, and breakfast and lunch sandwiches.

places.name: The Merchant at Joshua Ward House
Friendship Of Salem
places.description: A 171-foot replica of the 1797 East Indiaman Friendship, berthed at Derby Wharf. The three-masted tall ship recalls the world-spanning voyages that made Salem one of America's richest ports.

places.name: Red's Sandwich Shop
places.description: A Salem breakfast institution since 1945, serving classic diner fare from booths and a counter inside the historic London Coffee House, a Revolution-era meeting spot.

places.name: Modern Magic
places.description: A witch-owned shop and teaching studio that pairs magical tools and apparel with classes in the Craft — a place to buy your supplies and learn to use them.

places.name: Pentagram: Witchcraft & Magick Shoppe
places.description: A witch-run shop across from the Witch Trials Memorial, stocked with handmade tools, candles, oils, and jewelry crafted by local witches, with psychic and medium readings on offer.
Two attractions in one: wax tableaux of Salem's witch-trial and seafaring history, plus a walk-through witch village, steps from the Witch Trials Memorial.
places.name: Salem Wax Museum & Salem Witch Village

places.description: A 'dark romantic' boutique and independent bookstore opened in 2022, with curated books, artisan perfume, jewelry, and antiques arranged across a warren of atmospheric rooms.
places.name: Nocturne
Salem Museum Of Torture
places.description: A walk-through gallery of historical punishment devices — the rack, the iron maiden, and more — with life-size displays detailing centuries of grim European justice.

places.name: Jaho
places.description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

places.name: Jaho
places.description: A Salem-born specialty coffee roaster and café — espresso and tea by day, wine and cocktails by night, with beans roasted just up the road.

places.name: Howling Wolf Taqueria
places.description: A lively taqueria and cocktail bar on Lafayette Street, slinging tacos and margaritas, with plenty of vegan options, in a festive, colorful room.
A horror museum of sixty-plus life-size movie monsters, from Dracula to The Exorcist, sculpted by Hollywood effects artists. Cameras stay in your pocket inside the gallery.
places.name: Count Orlok's Nightmare Gallery

places.description: A family-friendly walk through six fantasy realms, from enchanted forest to dragon's lair, full of hidden, hands-on magic — a wizardly antidote to Salem's scarier stops.
places.name: Professor Spindlewink's World of Wizardry

places.description: A small square brick lighthouse from 1871 at the end of half-mile-long Derby Wharf, still flashing over Salem Harbor. The walk out to it is one of the city's finest waterfront strolls.
places.name: Derby Wharf Light Station

places.description: A guided walk past fifteen life-size scenes recreating the 1692 hysteria, from Tituba's kitchen to the gallows. One of Salem's trio of narrated witch-history attractions.
places.name: Witch History Museum

places.description: A two-story waterfront seafood spot on Pickering Wharf with a raw bar, harbor views, and a seasonal patio out over the marina.
places.name: Sea Level Oyster Bar
Salem Maritime National Historic Site
places.description: America's first National Historic Site (1938), preserving the wharves, Custom House, and tall ship that powered Salem's golden age of global sea trade. It was redesignated a National Historical Park in 2025.

places.name: Derby House
places.description: Salem's oldest brick house, built in 1762 by Captain Richard Derby for his son Elias, who would become one of America's first millionaires through the sea trade.

places.name: Far From The Tree Cider
places.description: Salem's hard-cider taproom near the train station, pouring flights of locally pressed apple cider in a family- and dog-friendly room.
An 1871 cast-iron lighthouse on Winter Island beside an old harbor fort. Dark for years, it was relit in 1983 and can be reached on foot through the park.
places.name: Fort Pickering Lighthouse

places.description: A chocolate house beside the Peabody Essex pouring historical drinking-chocolate 'elixirs,' from Mesoamerican to colonial recipes, alongside artisan truffles. Hours are limited.
places.name: Kakawa Chocolate House

places.description: A snug downtown coffeehouse since 1996 — organic espresso, teas, and sandwiches in what regulars fondly call 'Salem's living room.'
places.name: Front Street Coffeehouse

places.description: A cheeky, colorful seafood joint on Artists' Row, famous for its Lobstertini and a no-pretense menu of New England classics, with live music. Open seasonally.
places.name: The Lobster Shanty

places.description: A modern Mediterranean restaurant in the old Salem News building, with house-made bread and pasta, brick-oven pizza, and flavors from the Adriatic coast.
places.name: Adriatic Restaurant & Bar

places.description: A restored crescent of sand along Salem Willows facing Beverly Harbor. Its grim name dates to the 1850s, when the remote shore was used to dispose of dead horses.
places.name: Dead Horse Beach

places.description: A laid-back cocktail lounge known for vintage drinks, gourmet grilled cheese, and what may be the last standing CD jukebox in Salem.
places.name: All Souls Lounge

places.description: A small, calm neighborhood beach on Collins Cove with views across the water to Beverly. Sheltered shallows and an adjoining playground make it an easygoing local spot for families.
places.name: Collins Cove Beach
